In the last week of October 2004, with a main focus on another, different investigation, approximately 6.000 pages of material was made available to the Office of the Prosecutor in electronic format. The electronic format on which these documents were provided to the Office of the Prosecutor is not a system that is compatible with the current systems in operation by this Tribunal. The ITSS, that is the computer services here, are making efforts so that these documents can be completely and fully disclosed to the Defence to the extent that there's Rule 68 material. Again these documents in this collection all relate to 1995, so there would only be limited relevance. We are currently undertaking Rule 68 reviews of these materials but we're unable at this time to do so electronically because the system is not -- the format that was used by the Bosnian government is not one that's compatible with the electronic search tools we have here, which means we are in the process of going through the roughly 6.000 pages of material individually. And I simply alert the Chamber to that fact. Again, this specific document was disclosed, I believe late last week or certainly early this week. The Defence were notified in advance that we would be using it with either yesterday's witness or today's witness. I might also add, however, Mr. President, and it might be necessary to take a brief recess for this purpose, there is another document which our position would be, in light of what the witness has testified, particularly about the El Mujahedin detachment and the fact that it was not created in accordance with the -- or pursuant to the structure that he's described, we have another document which is not with us in the courtroom because the witness's answer was not one that we could predict based on the 65 ter summary in terms of denial that the El Mujahid detachment even existed. We would like to retrieve this new document, provide copies to the Defence and perhaps, depending on answers the witness might give during the cross-examination, we might, with the Chamber's leave, put that document to the witness. This is a document from December 1995 relating to the, in effect, disestablishment of the El Mujahedin detachment. There are two documents, my colleague informs me. There are two documents, one of them from the Supreme Command Staff to the commander of the 3rd Corps at the end of December 1995 to disestablish the El Mujadin detachment with very specific instructions as to how that disestablishment was to take place. Again I don't know because we haven't asked the witness but certainly at least in May of 1995, according to this document that I have before me now, this witness was a member of the 3rd Corps, and the document that I would like to show him, again, has been disclosed to the Defence but we do have two additional documents relating to the disestablishment of the El Mujahid detachment in December 1995 that we might like to show to the witness, but again, we don't have those documents in the courtroom for the simple reason that the 65 ter summary did not provide us with notice that this witness was going to testify about the El Mujahid detachment and the fact that it wasn't created in the time period set forth in the indictment. So those would be our submissions, Mr. President, on these potential new documents. And again, this would be the only area that we will be cross-examining the witness on, so I don't anticipate the cross-examination to take too long, but if we're granted leave, we may need to take a brief recess in order to retrieve these documents and provide them to the Defence, these additional two documents in addition to the one that's already been notified and disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'll give the floor to the Defence. However, before I do so, let me summarise the position of the Prosecution so that the Judges keep abreast of the problem. The Prosecution tells us that in October 2004, within the framework of their investigations, they found 6.000 documents coming from the security services of Bosnia-Herzegovina, entitled OSA. Among those documents, which are in electronic form but one that is incompatible with the Tribunal's system, the Prosecution was not able, pursuant to Rule 68, to disclose all these 6.000 documents to the Defence due to technical problems. Nevertheless, the Prosecution tells us that now, at 11.25, they have a document which they have communicated to the Defence and which they would like to show to the witness as part of a credibility test and a refreshing of his memory. Since the witness said in answer to one question that this unit, as far as he knew, never existed within the 3rd Corps, and the Prosecution wishes to confront him with the documents they have pursuant to our previous decision in which we said that the new document could be shown to a witness only to test his credibility or to refresh his memory. However, the Prosecution also wishes to show another document which supports its case and which they did not have time to prepare, for technical reasons, and they're requesting a short break to find it and show it to the Defence. So that is the position of the Prosecution. I should like to hear the opinion of the Defence now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in accordance with your decision and the fact that the Prosecution has given us a document which appears to come from this witness, we do not object that that document be used, but for the purposes clearly indicated in your decision; that is, to test the credibility of the witness or to refresh his memory. As far as the other documents are concerned, we object to them being shown to the witness because the Defence has not received any such documents and because the Prosecution, in its arguments, does -- has not said that they could be used for the same purposes as indicated by the decision of the Chamber. Accordingly -- according to what we heard, these documents are the result of additional investigations by the Prosecution. And finally, the Prosecution was not caught by surprise by the questions we put to this witness, because in the summary it is clearly said that his testimony would also relate to a later period when this unit of foreigners was formed and when they were placed under the army's control. And it is also stated that he would testify about the process of mobilisation, the problems, ID documents, and the other issues that the witness has testified about. Therefore, our summary does indicate what the witness testified about. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We have no objection either to the document that has been disclosed to us being shown to the witness, but we would ask that the Prosecution should clarify whether it is for the purposes of credibility or memory refreshing. In our view, those are very different concepts, and in terms of how Your Honours then review the evidence that is given thereafter, it's important whether it was shown to test the truth of what the witness was saying or whether it's shown simply to refresh his memory. Your Honour, in addition to that, there is another point that I do wish to raise given what my learned friend has said about 6.000 documents being discovered in October 2004 within the security services. This issue might arise again potentially if the Prosecution seeks to reopen its case or seeks to bring evidence in rebuttal, and I simply wish to say at this point that, in the Defence's submission, this is a large body of documentation which in our view should not be permitted to be introduced at such a late stage in the trial, in a way retrying many of the issues that have arisen already. And these are not documents, as we've discovered, that didn't exist at the time the investigation into this case commenced, 'way before 2001. There was a lengthy period of investigation, and in our view, the security services would have been one of the first places that the Prosecutor's office should have gone to, given the nature of this case, to seek evidence against the accused. So this material has been discovered very late in the day, and in our view that is an important point to bear in mind. It might be one that is raised later if there is a rebuttal argument put forward by the Prosecution. Your Honour, lastly in relation to the additional documents that we've heard about now, we haven't seen them. We would want an opportunity to do that, but I agree with my learned colleague Ms. Residovic that the Prosecution had ample notice that this witness would talk about matters related to the El Mujahid unit. In fact, that's why they had disclosed to us the first document, which we are not objecting to. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall give the floor to Mr. Mundis again, but there's a small point to be clarified in what the Defence is saying. Our decision authorises the Prosecution to produce a document to refresh memory or to test credibility. The refreshment means because the witness may have forgotten some things, but credibility is something quite different. Credibility is when a witness in good faith, or maybe in bad faith, asserts something. So one should make a clear distinction when a request is made to produce such a document whether it is being done to -- as a reminder or within the framework of testing the credibility of the witness. Having said that, the Chamber would also like to know, but we will deliberate about this amongst ourselves, this second document, is it really necessary in relation to the first document? Because if the first document achieves the desired goal, is it necessary to have a second document? As we are totally ignorant about those documents, this second document, is it not perhaps superfluous? If it is, it's not necessary, especially if it's being used to test credibility or refresh memory. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And I did want to -- I'll address that concern in just a moment, but I did want to either clarify or correct what I said before in the event it was mistaken. This collection contains 6.000 pages, not 6.000 documents. There might be a slight difference between the two. I believe I said pages, but if not, it's 6.000 pages of material. With respect to the -- to the point as to the difference between credibility and refreshing, again the Prosecution would submit that Your Honour has it exactly right. We can't say whether the document will be shown to challenge his credibility or refresh his recollection until the witness has the document. Once he has the document, he very well may say, "Oh, yes. I was mistaken. I do remember that now that I've seen this document," and then it's not necessarily an issue of credibility. So we really need to be able to put the document to him before we can make any kind of argument at a later point, once all the evidence is in, as to his credibility or not. With respect to the point raised by my learned colleague Mr. Dixon about when the material was obtained, at this point in time, Mr. President, I would reserve our comments on that, pending any type of motion, perhaps, to either reopen or to put on evidence in rebuttal. The fact that material existed in 2000 or 2001 does not necessarily mean that the person or agencies or governments who controlled that information would let us get to it, and I just leave it at that for now. Let me also say, Mr. President, that among one of the reasons why some of this material has not been disclosed, this entire collection, is again it relates to another investigation focusing on 1995, number one; number two, because of the large quantity of material, the Office of the Prosecution has not reviewed it all because it is in both the Bosnian language and there are within this collection a large number of documents in Arabic for which the Prosecution is seeking to have these documents translated as well. So there is a huge amount of material, it's not in a language that we're able to process -- or parts of it is not in a language that we are able to quickly process. We are taking all the necessary steps to identify potential rule 68 material for this case. And I will leave it all at that point in time, Mr. President. The final point with respect to two additional documents: You're absolutely right that we very well may not need to show the witness those documents, depending on his response to the first document. I simply raised it now so that we can deal with all of these issues in one go rather than having the cross-examination broken up repeatedly by objections, thus delaying it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think that in view of the time, the best thing to do would be for the witness to come back, to be questioned about the first document, because the Prosecution says that it is quite possible that they will not the second document. If that is so, after this first document, we can stop and have a break, allow the Prosecution to disclose those other documents if they need them. Mr. Usher, will you go and fetch the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Brigadier Hubo. My name is Daryl Mundis, and along with my colleagues here today, we represent the Prosecution in this case. We have some questions for you, but before I do that, sir, let me just inform you that it's not our intention in any way to confuse you, and in the event you don't understand any of my questions, just ask me and I'll clarify or rephrase the question for you. Sir, I would like to focus on the subject that you were discussing towards the end of the direct examination by my learned colleague Madam Residovic; that is the El Mujahedin detachment. I would like you to -- you told us, sir, that -- and this is at page 41, line 25, carrying on to page 42, line 2, in the English translation in response to a question about the El Mujahedin detachment, the answer was translated as: "I never came across the necessary documentation for that, neither was that unit mentioned in any of the reports or any document whatsoever." My question to you, sir, is: Did the El Mujahedin detachment -- was it ever created or was that unit never formed?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I have already said, and I speak from memory: During 1994 and 1995, up until the end of the war, there were attempts for that unit to be formed. I don't know if that answers your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I take it, then, that because you say there were attempts rather than the unit was formed, it's your testimony that those attempts were not successful.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: That depends. At the end of the war, at a certain point in time we had certain lists, lists of complete units including foreigners and locals, Bosnians. But this was a stage just prior to the end of the war. Why am I saying this? Because it was a very difficult situation. The foreigners were not mobilised in the way I've explained, but attempts were made to set them up like any other unit. That means that we should know the composition, the situation, all the data from the records, and those data should be forwarded to the competent defence departments responsible for records. I'm just talking about records, nothing else. I hope you won't take it that I'm referring to anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, again, I understand the testimony you've given us about these attempts at compiling lists, but my question, sir, is was the El Mujahedin or El Mujahid detachment ever actually created?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: It was never created like a normal unit. As I was saying, at a certain point in time there were attempts, and eventually some sort of a record was established. As far as the listing of men and their names, which were no secret, at the end of the war, these lists were forwarded to defence departments in accordance with the procedure prescribed for all units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And these lists, as you've told us at line 7 on page 56, this list of complete units, including foreigners, these foreigners had been part of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina prior to this time at the end of the war; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: It is hard for me to answer that question, whether somebody was part or not. I didn't have insight as I did in the case of normal units to see for myself. So I can only tell you about the things that I myself saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, in May of 1995, can you tell us what position you held within the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: At the time, if I'm not mistaken, I was assistant commander for organisational, mobilisation and personnel affairs. I think that was its name. It was part of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So in effect, sir, you were doing the same job in May of 1995 that you had been doing during 1993.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: More or less, with some minor differences in the range of duties that we had in 1995 and in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, these lists that were compiled in 1995, were you in fact responsible for producing these lists?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I was not responsible for compiling any kind of lists. The responsibility of the corps command was to keep individual records for members of the corps command and staff units. Lists were compiled and forwarded by units of a certain level. Those who were not within the command, to make myself quite clear, that body - I wasn't alone; there were ten men in that department - we were not responsible nor was it our duty to count people and to take data from those people and to make a record of their names. This was the regular procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you certainly, from subordinate units of the 3rd Corps, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. received this information and compiled this information and forwarded this information up the chain of command, did you not?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: In a stage when the corps was better organised and in the desire to carry out a more complete check-up, we had lists -- or, rather, we required various information from units - among other things, lists of personnel - for various reasons, such as packages, logistics, finances and so on. I say again that those lists, in 1995, were given to us, and we had a kind of database for other units, and we wanted to improve our efficiency by producing in computerised form information about the units and their personnel for the needs of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And with respect to the foreigners, where you knew it you also put the country of origin of these people, is that right, on these lists?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I did not have the opportunity to check or see. I wish to underline that once again. We started to receive some sort of lists. Why am I saying this? Because there were a number of such lists. Each time they differed from the previous time, which was an indication that they were rather poor, and that's why I'm saying that there was an effort to improve the situation. But the possibilities were very limited, at least as far as my body, which should have had a record, is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, I understand that your role as the assistant commander was not one where you would personally be verifying such information, but you certainly relied upon the subordinate units in referring or reporting this information to you, and you compiled this information and sent it up the chain of command, did you not?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: So we did have information from the units, that they gave to us, and those were the data available to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And among the data that the various units reported to you was the date of entry of these foreigners into the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: For most units, I say again the database was far more detailed, and among other elements this one should be included, the date, place, date of birth and all personal information, and among other things also when that individual joined the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, did you compile such a list for the El Mujahedin detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific? Why am I saying that? I did not compile anything. For El Mujahid and for other units we did provide data that were given to us. I didn't do anything on my own. Then I would have introduced certain elements myself. This was simply copying what we received from subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I understand, sir, that you didn't compile the lists, but did you report or did you put your name on a document going up the chain of command concerning the El Mujahedin detachment and its members, including foreigners, and among the foreigners individuals who had been in the ABiH 3rd Corps from 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Of course I did, as in the case of other units, whoever made such a request from us. Our intention and wish was to finalise those lists, and these were attempts in relation to the defence department with which no contacts had been established to compare the data we had. So this was an additional effort on the part of the corps command in this particular case. So as for other units, let me mention the situation at the time. We had dead among our casualties, and in 1993 and 1994, we didn't even know who was in the corps command. And family members would inquire about someone, and then we would send a dispatch to all units to report back to us. However, in this way, it was easier for us to communicate. We were more operational. So this is just an illustration of our efforts to find out what the actual numerical situation was and to have exact records.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Among the lists or the list that was compiled for the El Mujahedin detachment, how many of those people whose names were on that list were foreigners?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I answer from memory. Complete lists -- can I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I pointed out that those lists varied from 100 men of that extraction, that is people who were not from the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina or from ex-Yugoslavia, it varied from 100 up to 200 something at the end of the war. All those lists with such data, the data being those that were provided to us, were then compiled according to procedure and then sent back to the Ministry of Defence. So that list exists in the present Ministry of Defence department in Zenica, and then people can address certain problems on the basis of those lists. However, the exact records, in my view, was something that we were never to -- able to fully verify.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, based on the best recollection that you have, at the time you joined the 3rd Corps in June of 1993, how many foreigners of Middle East or African descent were in units of the 3rd Corps, the subordinate units of the 3rd Corps? How many Middle East and African foreigners were in the ABiH 3rd Corps when you arrived in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I joined the command of the 3rd Corps before June, and I wasn't working on that. It wasn't within my terms of reference at all. So as far as municipal staffs are concerned, I didn't come across a single such member. As for others, I said once I took up my duties in the corps when we first started to receive some sort of lists. Of course I am speaking to the best of my recollection about events that took place more than ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, to the best of your recollection, when you joined the 3rd Corps, how many Middle East and African foreigners were in the ABiH 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: When I joined the command of 3rd Corps, I was not aware of any one, any single one. The work I did didn't show me that. If you're asking me whether I saw people on the ground, I did see them as members of various humanitarian organisations, but I cannot answer that question whether he was a member of the army or not because I simply don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that when you arrived at the 3rd Corps, this was not part of your duties. You weren't working on the issue. It wasn't within your terms of reference. Was there someone within the personnel office of the 3rd Corps who was responsible for these foreigners or compiling information on foreigners that might have been in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: As far as I know, the main body in charge of foreigners was the MUP. We in the 3rd Corps had a security organ which I assume should have had some insight. I specifically did not, was not involved in that segment. I did not interfere in their activities, but I supported them as much as I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let me -- when I'm talking now, sir, about these foreigners, I'm talking about foreigners who were in units of the 3rd Corps, in its subordinate units. Was there someone within the personnel office of the 3rd Corps who was responsible for obtaining information such as personnel information on the foreigners?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness has already answered several questions from my learned friend that when he joined the 3rd Corps he was not aware of a single foreigner in the 3rd Corps. All the following questions are not based on the answers given by the witness so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, we're -- the witness said it wasn't within his terms of reference. My only question is if there was someone -- he was the assistant commander for personnel, organisational matters, if there was someone in the office who was responsible for compiling the information. That's the only question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite so. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, within the personnel office of the 3rd Corps, was there a specific individual who was responsible for obtaining information about foreigners that were in units of the 3rd Corps? And when I say "information," I'm talking about date of birth, place of birth, country of nationality, passport details, et cetera. Was there someone within the 3rd Corps, from the personnel point of view, who was responsible for obtaining this information from the subordinate units of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I think one time your question was in the organ of the body of which I was the chief and another time the 3rd Corps. My answer is that in my organ, no one was specially assigned to keeping a record of foreigners. However, in the 3rd Corps command I assume it should have been the duty of the military security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, were there -- again, let me go back and stress this point: Were there foreigners from the Middle East and Africa in units of the 3rd Corps in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: As far as I know, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the new document at this point be shown to the witness. We do have copies. Again, because of the electronic formatting issue, these documents do not as yet have ERN numbers on them. This is a document dated 7 May 1995. We are also awaiting the English translation of the document, but I will lead the witness through the columns and the text of the document. And perhaps if the usher could, once he's done, if the document perhaps could be put on the ELMO for the benefit of the language booths.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, can I ask you to take a look at the last page of this document. Sir, is that -- is this a document that bears your name as being the person who submitted the document?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Yes. It says here my name on this document without a signature, but it's not contestable. The EH are probably the initials of a young man who had the database or kept records and sent it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you now look at the first page of this document, at the top, and can you tell us, sir, if this is one of the lists that you've been telling us about.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 7th of May, 1995. It is -- the list is being sent to the department of the military security department. It says: "At your request, we attach to the document a list of members of the El Mujahedin detachment, persons of foreign nationality." So this is one of the lists, one of many that we sent on to the SVB or department of military security for some reason which I can't tell you now. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. So all the persons who are listed on this document, there are 252 names, these are all foreigners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I haven't had a look at them all, but I assume that they are foreigners, yes, people of foreign origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, sir, I'm basing this on what you just read to us, that it says at your top: "At your request, we attach to the document a list of the members of the El Mujahedin detachment, persons of foreign nationality." Is that what the document says?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: You read out what it says on the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you now, sir, if you could look at the column, the headings on the columns, and if you could tell us what those different columns, the headings of those columns represent.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: It says here the number, surname, name, date of birth, place and municipality of birth, "in the army since," and "in the records since," or "registered as of."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, have you seen this document before today?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, this is a document that you sent to the military security service, is that right, in 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Probably. Obviously it is a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You just told us a few moments ago that you were not aware of any foreigners being in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992 and 1993. Is that what you told us?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I couldn't have known, functionally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. But you certainly have reported to the military security service that such persons were in units of the ABiH in 1992 and 1993. That's what your document indicates; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: In this document, you have a list of people, the list that we received from the unit, which means -- I'm saying again that this is a copied document with information, data which was sent in to us from that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, sir, my question wasn't exactly whether you personally checked any of these records. My question was whether you were aware -- and that awareness could come from a variety of sources, including the subordinate units that reported to you. You were absolutely aware, based on this document, that there were a number of foreigners who were in the ABiH from the middle of 1992 onwards.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that, sir. I cannot confirm that or the data here. According to me, I wouldn't say they were correct. This is one of the documents which was probably -- it was probably an attempt to ascertain the state of affairs. I don't know what this name means, Ebu this or that, for me to be able to provide a comprehensive information to you, either then or now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir -- but this is a document that you told us -- I asked you if you sent it to military security in 1995, and you said probably, and so I'm a bit confused as to -- you told us that you probably sent this document up to military security, and the document on its face indicates a number of foreigners who were in the ABiH from at least August 1992, and now you're telling us that you weren't aware of the information in a document that you probably sent.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I'm speaking on the basis of the units, the units that we had at our disposal, normal units and their reports, whereas this document, this is a report of this particular unit, and what they say, that they were there as of that date, I'm not sure it was valid for me either then or now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, if you look at the last two columns, again the first column says "in the army from," and can you remind me what the last column says?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: The last column is "registered as of" or "in the records since." So that means that this should have been in the records of the unit, under normal circumstances, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just ask you, then, for example, number 4 on the list: Abdela Al Faruk; date of birth 2 March, 1969; place of birth Libya; in the ABiH since 5 August, 1992; as reflected in the records of the unit, 1 May 1993. You're telling us, sir, that you were not aware that you yourself were probably reporting this information to the military security?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Let me tell you, the data listed here is one thing, but I have my reasons to doubt these data. I think they are incomplete and incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: Why did you report information up the chain of command to the military security if you doubted the accuracy or completeness of this information?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. The interpreter I believe said I have reason to doubt. I have reason to doubt.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know why they asked me for this, whether I asked them to check it out because of my doubts or because of the lack of data and information. I cannot answer with any precision at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, I don't see anywhere in the document, sir - correct me if I'm wrong - but I don't see anywhere in the document where you informed the military security that you personally have doubts about the accuracy or completeness of this information. Did you notify them of that?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Probably I did, but we did not have reporting -- we had reporting with the commanders, and there were probably discussions about the problems that arose, and probably in this part, too, in this part of the work that I did too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But it's certainly not reflected in the document. You didn't tell military security, "I'm forwarding you some information on the El Mujahedin detachment and its foreign nationals, but I doubt whether this information is accurate or correct." You don't say that in the document.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: That doesn't exist in the document, no, but I am reproducing for you roughly the aspirations and what was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall on how many occasions you went back to the subordinate units and expressed disbelief to them as to the accuracy of the information? Did you ever go back to the assistant commanders for the brigades, the assistant commanders for personnel and say, "I don't believe this information you're sending me"?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Well, not that we did it once. We had regular meetings, if I can say so, of the professional organs. We had control and supervision in the units, which were based on correct data and tallying the correct data with the brigades and units. And we did this on several occasions by what we called a control, of one file with another, comparing file with file. For each conscript, for example, they had a file in one department and a file in the brigade and then all these files would be taken and compared file by file, all the information and data with the actual situation in the units on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what exactly at these meetings did you tell the subordinate units about the accuracy of this information or the completeness of this type of information? You told them that you doubted this information they were reporting to you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Well, every control implies verifying the data presented to the units, the report and what we called assistance, back-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we're understanding each other here, sir, but let me try this one more time. The document you have before you is based on information that you got from the personnel offices of the subordinate units of the 3rd Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: That means that I did not receive the information but it was sent by the unit command and the corps command, to make matters clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. The unit -- the subordinate units sent this information to the 3rd Corps, and you compiled the information and forwarded it to military security; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Well, I didn't send it on to the military security. I didn't forward the list of all the units to the military security. I forwarded it when necessary. At one point in time, we had what we called fictitiously compiled lists - and I can explain that to you - and then the service would check this out through its own chain, whether someone had been recorded and registered or not whereas they weren't in fact in the army. So it was a sort of abuse that went on. And this was a sort of way of helping out, whether we -- the data had been compiled as was requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you, sir, if the information contained in the document before you was obtained from the personnel departments of the subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that this information that's contained in the document, you have some doubts about the accuracy or completeness of this information. Is that what you've told us?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I told you. They are not complete, and I doubt them. I doubted them then and I doubt that they are correct information today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And my question, then, sir, is these doubts that you say you had both -- you have doubts today and you had doubts then, my question is: Did you communicate those doubts back to the personnel offices who provided you with the information?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: There was no Personnel Department of these. They were usually individuals -- an individual, and these individuals changed, and they would send out what they deemed fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection, sir, of -- again, there are 252 names on this document. Do you have any idea which subordinate units of the 3rd Corps these persons were in in 1992 and 1993, the ones who are listed as being in the army in 1992 and 1993? Do you have any recollection what units they were in?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I have no such information. There would have to have been some data if there were such persons in such units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, this list that, as you've told us, contains the names of foreigners who were in the El Mujahedin detachment, when was this unit, the El Mujahedin detachment, formally disbanded?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't present. At the time I was in Zenica, and the official deportation of those foreigners or the majority of them was after the Dayton agreement. They were deported in organised fashion. I think that they were deported from Bosnia through Croatia and further on, I don't know where to. And of course a portion of them stayed on respecting the citizenship of whatever the citizenship was, but I can't give you an exact date just off my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The -- but I'm referring now, sir, to the formal disbanding of the El Mujahedin detachment. That occurred in accordance with the Dayton agreement; did it not?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I can't say for sure. I really can't be certain. To the best of my recollection, well, I don't know. I think you have lists given to the Ministry of Defence departments in Zenica, so the date exists there, the exact date when they finished registering them or that unit, how long they were there for, until when.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, as part of the disbanding or disbandment of that unit, what steps were taken?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: As far as my part is concerned, if I can put it that way, my duties, my part of the job, commissions were set up pursuant to orders from our Supreme Command in each unit. There was a commission in each unit, and it was composed of, I think, four members, a four-member commission which compiled a list and then concluded that list and handed it over to the competent authorities in the Ministry of Defence. That's what I can say pursuant to my terms of reference and the job I was doing -- or, rather, my organ was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know what happened to the records or documents of the El Mujahedin detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Which documents do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Any -- any documents of that unit; orders, personnel records.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, if you mean foreigners, I don't know nor did I ever have occasion to see any of their documents. Now, what was the duty -- now, if this was done I can't tell you, I didn't check it out, is the defence department must have had an additional file for persons of that kind and then probably conclude that kind of list, but I never had occasion to see any file like that or anything else regarding that like in the other corps units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see any -- do you recall ever seeing any orders or documents requesting the 3rd Corps to burn or destroy records, stamps, seals, or any other type of material or equipment relating to the El Mujahedin detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember the details, so on the basis of my memory, there were -- all the units that were disbanded and had a stamp were duty-bound to return that, and then that was destroyed by the commission, that is to say with minutes kept and so on. As far as the other documents concerned, no, quite the contrary. We insisted, in fact. That is to say, the service I was in, we were fully conscious of what would follow; that is, the realisation of various rights and other things, and so we did our best to send the lists or, rather, to have this -- these records kept and established about all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, during 1995, did you ever see any documents relating to the El Mujahedin detachment that were in Arabic?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: It is difficult for me now to answer that question. I don't remember. There were orders, there were other documents of this nature, but I really don't remember. We don't know Arabic. And so let me repeat once again, as for this part I didn't know what this meant, this Ebu. What does Ebu mean? And somebody can't be called -- in a list you can't have somebody with Ebu there because it's not a first or last name. And there's a lot else that for me is quite incomprehensible, gibberish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time. This might be the appropriate time for the next technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's 12.25. We're going to take a technical break. Mr. Mundis, with respect to the second document, the Judges might wish to confer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's one of the issues that I'll be dealing with at the break with the Defence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As I was saying, it's 12.25. We reconvene at around ten minutes to one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Brigadier Hubo, thank you for answering our questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give the floor now to the Defence for additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, I will ask you a few questions linked to the questions and documents shown to you by the Prosecutor during the cross-examination. Do you have the document in front of you, Mr. Hubo?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Yes, I do -- no, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the document be provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you were the -- in the organisational, mobilisational and personnel department even in 1995, when, as you said, you had certain lists about the partial structure of the Mujahedin unit, can you tell me first who comprised that unit? Were they only foreigners, only locals, or both?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: According to the lists we were provided by that unit, there were foreigners of various origin, Eastern origin, and there were also local people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at this document now. A moment ago you said that all subordinate units would submit to the corps command lists which the corps command requested from them, is that right, regarding the composition of units?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: We didn't need all those lists from all the units, but in 1995, we had some computerised possibilities to print out the lists, because the corps at the time had more than 35.000 men. So it was not possible to check each and every file and list.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you get this list from which you forwarded on the 7th of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I assume that the information on the list was obtained from that unit. It may have included local people, but the young man working on this probably separated the foreigners from the locals, as they were probably the object of interest.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said from that unit. Can you tell us, which unit did you get this information from?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: From the El Mujahedin unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you look at the title of this document, please. What is the subject of this document?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: It says "List," a list of personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To whom are you forwarding it?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: It says "To the military security department of the 3rd Corps."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend asked you and suggested that you had forwarded it up the chain of command to the military security. Was this forwarded to a 3rd Corps department or to superior commands?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: This is probably addressed to the department of the military security service. There were other lists made, and whoever asked us for a list of records, we would provide them such lists. This applied to logistics and finances. But summary reports without any lists would go to superior commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the first sentence that you have already read out and which my learned friend read out to you also, there's indication why you are forwarding this list. Was it on your own initiative or is it not clear from this that such a list was requested from you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: It is clear that it is being provided at the request of the military security service. I am commenting on the document. Of course such information was available to anyone who needed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Anyone looking at this list can easily count, which I did, and see that in this column with the heading "In the army since," there is just over a hundred people who were allegedly in the ABiH in 1992 or 1993. Since you took over duties in the department for organisational and personnel affairs in the autumn of 1993, in that body did you come across information about a single foreigner in the units of the BH army in the autumn of 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, I had no survey of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, after the district Territorial Defence Staff was abolished, you moved to the command of the 3rd Corps, and you were in charge of certain activities linked to municipal Territorial Defence staffs. Tell me, during that period of time did you ever receive from any single Territorial Defence Municipal Staff any written information or by going to any municipal territorial staff or its anti-sabotage detachment, did you come across a single foreigner from Afro-Asian countries? Did you ever find out that in the territorial staffs and their units there were any foreigners?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I specifically did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said, Mr. Hubo, that performing your duties regarding territorial structures, that is municipal staffs, before you took up the duties linked to organisation and mobilisation, you also worked in the staff as an operative. During your activities as an operatives officer, did you ever, in 1993, find that in -- there were foreigners from Afro-Asian countries in any of the units of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I specifically was not one who was supposed to look into that, but Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I didn't come across any such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back a little to the method of work that you described in answer to questions from my learned colleague. You were asked whether you verified, in a sense, the work of your bodies in subordinate units, in brigades and operative groups, et cetera, and as far as I remember, you said of course we did, we had regular meetings, et cetera. Is my understanding of your answer correct?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Yes. That was one of the ways of checking the structure. I must say that at those meetings, the participants were not Bosniaks alone. There were many Serbs and Croats engaged in this kind of work in the units, and they can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood your answer correctly, you said that in the El Mujahedin detachment, then or later in 1994, 1995, there was no such structure.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I don't know at all what they had. I told you that they would send an individual, and these individuals changed. I didn't know what his position was or who he was except what he himself said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This individual, and it wasn't always the same one, would he attend regular meetings that you had with regular units of the ABiH when discussing problems related to your activities?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: That individual was -- I remember one of them. He was not an Arab. We wanted to make a record, and a local person would come who was from that unit. So I can't tell you that he was quite in the same capacity as the others. So I have photographs. I would have to remind myself, but I am not sure. This was more passive participation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the chief of a department or any one of your staff members, and there was some ten of them, could any one of them ever go to the El Mujahedin, the unit, and check out the situation in that unit?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Neither I nor any one of my subordinates could go to that unit and check it out. We simply had no access.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To go back to this list for a moment, you said that you received it from the El Mujahedin detachment. And all the information contained in that list was provided by whom?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I said that this was a copy of the information we received from the representative of that unit and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, this fourth column, under the heading "In the army since," did you receive this column from the El Mujahedin as well or did you get these dates from any other unit of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I wish to underline once again that this is a simple copy of data received. We had no possibilities or means of changing anything or adding or subtracting anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To make it quite clear, who did you get that data from?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: From that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, did you ever -- from the time you took up your duties in autumn 1993, did you ever receive from another unit, a brigade, a detachment, a Municipal Staff, or operations group, did you ever receive a list of names of their unit indicating that they had among their personnel foreign fighters?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I do not remember that happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In answer to my learned friend, you said that then and now you are doubting the truthfulness of the information contained here. In view of the fact that this document was requested from you by the military security organ and you said that they possibly could verify certain data, the fact that the security organ is asking you for information about foreigners in the El Mujahedin, does that confirm your doubts or does it indicate something else?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: They asked me for this for their own needs. Now, what those needs were was not something I inquired into, nor was it my duty. But I repeat again that I assume they wanted this information for their own needs, but also, in order to structure things properly, we asked for accurate and relevant data to have complete records of everything, as required by regulation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you received the list from El Mujahedin, tell me, did El Mujahedin provide you with attachments from which you might see whether these persons were in the army at all; and if so, in which unit?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: In that period of time, this was the maximum we could obtain from them. No supporting information could we receive nor did we receive indicating what you have just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend told you, since you expressed doubt as to the truthfulness of the dates regarding since when they were in the army, he told you that you did not express those doubts in this document, and you confirmed that. My question to you is: Is there your statement in this document that these data are correct and verified?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I don't know that there is such a statement by me anywhere, because I am now expressing doubts about many of the facts listed in this document and in lists provided by other units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we now look at these columns that have been filled in and given to you as the maximum they could do, the first column is the ordinal number, the second column gives first and last -- last and first names of the persons who were allegedly members of the El Mujahedin. On the 7th of May, 1995, when this document was compiled, were you convinced and did you know that these persons listed were all in the El Mujahedin detachment; and secondly, were they the real first and last names of these people?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I'm never -- I was never sure about who those people were nor what they were nor since when they were there. So for me, these data were always irrelevant. And my doubts proved true after the war, and I can give you some illustrations which can be verified. When the final list compiled by the unit and given to the Defence Department and a name that was given when they were to obtain certain entitlements regarding citizenship and marriages, et cetera, for the people who remained, they came back to the municipal authority and said, "I am not the person on that list, but that is how I was registered," which only shows that all these data were inaccurate and irrelevant. I said, for instance, Ebu this and Ebu that, as a lay Bosnian, doesn't mean anything to me. But surely a hundred people cannot be called Ebu. We are laymen, but by any analysis would show that this cannot reflect the true state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, the third column gives the date of birth. On the 7th of May, 1995, did you have any knowledge or conviction or the possibility to verify whether the people with these names were indeed born on the dates indicated under column "Date of birth"?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I had no possibility of verifying a single piece of information. If -- I say that I couldn't verify any of these data or columns, nor was it possible to do that. These were data received, copied, and as such, forwarded on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you did know or you were able to verify column 4. Somewhere you have the name of the town, sometimes the name of the country indicating where the people were coming from.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I underline once again that for many there is no indication of their place of birth or even country. In some cases some countries are mentioned, and what I just said applies to this as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you have commented on the first column in answer to my questions, is that the reason why, in answer to my learned friend, you said that you are not at all aware that the column headed "In the army since" could be true? Did you have any possibility of verifying that column?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I said once that different lists were submitted at different times. And if all those lists were to be compared, you would find differences. This column, "In the army since," was one that we were not able to verify.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also told my learned friend that after the Dayton Accords, the request was made to disband this unit, that most of the members were deported. Tell me, not in the army but in the political sphere, were there certain attempts and requirements on the part of these persons and people close to them to allow them to stay in the country?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I can't give you an expert opinion, but I can tell you on the basis of what I heard from people working in the administration. There were quite a number of people who on the basis of this, marriages and some other legal grounds, tried to retain some sort of status and remain in the country, and these lists probably are an indication of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, in the course of your duties, were you aware that citizenship could be acquired by establishing the fact that someone was a member of the army before May 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I never gave any thought to the matter in those days nor was it within my sphere of interest.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But working within the Defence Ministry, did you learn of that?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Yes. Talking to colleagues working in some other departments in the administration, in those cases, too, they complained that they were encountering the same difficulties, that the final list provided at the end of the war, as I explained, again the same problems arose, that the man may not be the one from the list, but he may claim that he was, or someone else, and then there was a whole procedure to establish the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And my final question, Mr. Hubo: After you had this list provided by the El Mujahedin and after all the questions put to you in connection with that document, can you tell me whether your knowledge, not your opinion any more, shows that foreigners or, rather, Mujahedin were not part of the 3rd Corps in 1993, and is that opinion unchanged?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: As far as foreigners are concerned, my opinion remains unchanged on the basis of my own personal experience, my recollection, and so on. Finally, I think that these people abused the institution of the army. The way in which this document was compiled shows that they did not respect the system or our own values as they were prescribed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions on behalf of Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Colonel, as far as I'm concerned, I have several questions to ask you. Would you take up the document again, please. You should have it in front of you. And may we have the document placed on the overhead projector, please, Mr. Usher, with your assistance. Now, looking at the document, could you tell me what it says at the top to the left? There are some figures and the date, and afterwards -- above that it says 05/4-1028. What does that number represent?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: That number denotes the number which was given to the department in the protocol book, book of protocols.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And your service, what number did it have in the book of protocols?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: My service was 05. That was its number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You say your service had 05 as its number. Now, what about the 4, /4? What does the 4 stand for? 05/4.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I can't tell you now. It means that it was recorded in the protocols book, a certain subject, lists, requests. They were given numbers according to the groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Different categories. Right. Now, to the best of your recollection, category 1, what was that? Categories 1, 2, 3 and 4, what category was 4?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I really couldn't say with any certainty whether this denoted a category of documents or not. I'm not quite sure. I'm sorry, I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You can't tell me. Now, what about the 1028 figure? What's that? What does that tell you? Does it tell you anything? In category 4, was the 1.028th document, or what? What is 1028 number? What does it signify?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I assume it ought to be what you've just said. That is to say, at the beginning of the year a book of protocols is opened up, and the first numbers are assigned according to the groups or categories. So this is -- the first number is the category number and this is the number given to the document or list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now will you turn to the last page of the document and look at the last page, please, just the last page. Since we don't have the English translation of the document, we're going to rely on what you tell us. We have EH/EH in the left column. What is this EH/EH, capitals?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: At the time, this first EH was placed before the dash, and that was usually the document -- the person who compiled the document. And after the dash, or forward slash, were the initials of the individual who typed out the document. I think that in this case, it was Emir Hurem. So he compiled the document and typed it out. It would be the same man, I assume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So that's the person who compiled the document typed it up. Now, underneath, in your language, it sales "Dostavljeno." What is the translation of that? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Well, we write who the document is sent out to, delivered to, and it says "Title," "Naslovu," and then the "a/a" on behalf of the organ or commander. It's not signed, but that doesn't matter. Sometimes they are signed and not signed, but this expresses what I have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you say that a/a, a/a is the person who acts for the commander. The archives, does that mean archives? Normally in military terms, the addressees, you have a list of the persons to whom the document is delivered to, and the a/a, you say that that is the person who reacts on the part of the commander. Why is that in the list of addressees?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I don't know if I'm understanding you properly. The left-hand column, it says "Dostavljeno," "delivered to," and then it says "title" "Naslovu." "Naslovu" means the title on the first page of the document. Here it says the SVB -- "Odjeljenje SVB," or "Department SVB." And then the archives. "A/a" means archives, that a copy is sent to the archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I thought. Thank you. Now we have it. So a/a is archives. Now, let's look at the left hand -- the right-hand side. What does it say there? And I'm reading PK ZA OM I KP? What does all that mean?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: It is the function, the post in the command of the 3rd Corps linked to this protocol number 05 at the top on the first page. On the first page, that document in the upper left-hand corner, the 05.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, can it happen that your Emir Hurem, the EH might have written your name down but might not have shown you this document, or do you remember having seen the document? Because there is not signature. So you are not the intellectual author of the document. So my question to you is this, to make things quite clear: Could the document have gone -- passed you by without you having seen it, actually seen it yourself?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Hypothetically, everything is possible, Your Honour. I had 50 or 60 documents that I would have to look at on a daily basis and sign and distribute and so on. I see no reason, therefore, with this one. I assume that this is the database that we had and which was sent to us as it was, and then it was sent on. So I have no reason to doubt that somebody wanted to plant this on me or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, would you say, looking at the text, that this was typewritten on a typewriter or on a computer? What can you say looking at the form of type, the letters, the type?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I assume that this was compiled on a computer. We actually just had one typewriter that we wrote some other documents on, typed them out on that one typewriter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say this is a computer. Right. Now, that computer, we're talking about 1995. It's probably disappeared in the meantime, but let's go on to another subject. Let's move on. When you yourself were a member of the 3rd Corps, how were you paid? Did you receive a salary at the end of the month or not or no salary, or how did this function? How were you paid? I ask you this because the Defence showed you P192 where there was a paragraph on salaries and problems of payment. So how were you paid at the time? Were you paid in dinars, in Deutschmarks? Were you paid through an account or in cash or how -- how did you get your salary?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know when we actually started receiving a sort of salary in cash. I think at the time I had ten marks, ten Deutschmarks. The soldiers had 20 Deutschmarks. Now, from the 6th of April, I think it was, until Dayton was signed, the Dayton agreement was signed in Paris, and the Paris agreement, we were issued certificates, and for every month spent in the army, you would have 400 Deutschmarks paid out to you in the form of a certificate. That is to say 400 marks on paper, not in cash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But when you received ten marks or 20 marks, was that at the end of the month, beginning of the month, middle of the month? When?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly but lists were compiled for that, too, for the money, remuneration we received. There were lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who actually supplied the money? Who in the 3rd Corps -- or, rather, who in the 3rd Corps gave you the money or paid the soldiers of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: The money was supplied, as far as I know, by the government via the General Staff at the time and the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, yes. But was there somebody in the 3rd Corps, a military officer, who distributed the money to you? Was somebody in charge of distributing the actual money to you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: In the 3rd Corps command there was an organ or department for material and financial matters, and in each brigade there was a man like that, too, to deal with financial matters and see to things of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if the person handing -- the person handing out the money, would they do that on the basis of a list they had?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: That person did have a list supplied by the command. The command compiled the list. The command of the unit, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And is that what happened in all the units? Is that the way they were paid in all the units?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: At the time, as far as I know, that was what the custom was. That was how we were paid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, after -- following my questions, would the parties like to ask any additional questions? Mr. Mundis, you first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just have one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you still have the document? No. The Presiding Judge asked you a question about -- I'm looking at the back of the document right above where your name appears, the initials PK and then the word ZA OM I KP that actually stands for assistant commander for -- can you tell us what that stands for?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: For organisational, mobilisational, and cadres affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Personnel.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Or personnel affairs, yes, cadres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That phrase is actually an abbreviation for the position that you held in 1995? Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give the floor to the Defence for any final questions they may have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: No questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, on behalf of the Chamber, I would like to thank you for having come to The Hague and testified and answered the questions from the Defence and also from the Prosecution, as well as questions from me, too. I asked you to clarify certain points, so I thank you for that. On behalf of the Chamber, I wish to express our best wishes for a safe return back home, and I hope you have every success in your military career. The usher will now escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, as regards the document or the documents, because the Defence provided us with a binder. First the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we would like to tender into evidence as Defence documents the following: Number 2 on our list, which is 1381; then number 8, 1407; and document number 10, to be marked for identification because we just have the document in the Bosnian Herzegovinian version, and it is the decree on the criteria and normatives, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Mundis, what about the two documents, 1407 and the other one? What is your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, may we have the three numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. So we have two documents admitted into evidence. They are DH1381, with the English version being 1381/E. Then DH1407, and the English version DH1407/E. The third document is a document marked for identification. That number will be DH2015 ID. The date is the 26th of October, 1992, and it is titled in English, provisional title [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... Normative on a Disposition of Citizens and Resources in the Armed Forces and Other Needs of Defence. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Now, the Prosecution. Any documents there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We would respectfully request that the document which we showed to the witness bearing the date 7 May 1995 be admitted into evidence with the notation as per the earlier documents, that it goes to credibility and/or refreshing recollection. We will provide an English translation for the document as quickly as possible. I am aware that normally we've been marking documents until we have the translation. That's fine. If we simply want it marked for identification with that note and then once we provide the translation it could then be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For identification. Right. I turn to the Defence. A number marked for identification with the usual markings. No objections there? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: No objections, only to say as a matter of principle that there's been a lot of testimony given about this document and that it can only be used for credibility or refreshing memory, not as part of the Prosecution case. But I would return to the point that I made earlier that it would be helpful, I think, for Your Honours if the Prosecution could say on what basis do they introduce it; credibility or refreshing memory? It's of course for Your Honours to decide in reviewing the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: -- but the Prosecution wasn't absolutely clear on that. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But the Prosecution agreed on that point completely. Now, Mr. Registrar, may we have a number for -- marked for identification, because we need the English translation, and to mark it credibility test or refreshment of memory pursuant to the decision we took a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Yes. You've said it all. This document, therefore, is marked for identification, and the number with the proviso as mentioned, to refresh memory or to test the credibility, P950 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going into private session for a few moments now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there are no matters outstanding, we adjourn the meeting and reconvene next week on Monday at quarter past two. I wish you a very good weekend and hope to see you back here on Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 7th day of February, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
